statement: https://www.humblebundle.com/ is the canonical origin; the apex and http variants 301 to it and Cloudflare fronts every response.

Pages are server-rendered shells (head, announcement banner, navbar, footer) that hydrate their main content from embedded JSON state blobs (base-webpack-json-data, landingPage-json-data, webpack-bundle-page-data, storefront-webpack-json-data, storefront-constants-json-data, webpack-choice-marketing-data).

Primary navigation is Bundles / Store / Choice / Blog / About with hover mega-menu panels (.nav-dropdown-container holding .navbar-item-dropdown-container, opened by setting display:block); the Store panel has four columns (Popular, Top Genres, Top Platforms, Featured).
/login and /signup are client-rendered SPA shells; their fields, SSO buttons and captcha are injected by JS, so the frozen clone serves their post-render DOM.
Password recovery has no standalone URL: /forgot and /reset-password are SPA soft-404s and recovery is an in-page 'Password Reset' state on /login.
The authenticated area lives under /home/*; anonymous requests to /home/library, /home/purchases and /home/keys redirect 302 to /login?goto=<original-path>&qs=reason%3DsecureArea.
There is no /cart page route (the source returns 404); the cart is a client-side drawer bounded by MAX_CART_SIZE 20 and MAX_WISHLIST_SIZE 100, and checkout lives at /checkout.

The first-party store API is GET /store/api/search (params filter, genre, platform, drm, search, sort, page, developer, publisher; sorts discount|alphabetical|newest|bestselling; page_size 20) plus GET /store/api/lookup?products[]=<slug>; Cloudflare rejects tokenless clients, so harvesting required a real browser fingerprint.

Header search suggestions are served client-side by Algolia (index replica_product_query_site_search) and render as .product-search-result rows inside .site-search-results; the clone reimplements the panel locally against its own catalog.

Help is a Zendesk Help Center on the same registrable domain (support.humblebundle.com/hc/en-us) with category and article levels; plain HTTP clients hit a Cloudflare challenge there while a real browser passes.

The anchor bundle /games/yes-chef-cooking-bundle has three cumulative pay-what-you-want tiers at CA$9.71 (7 items), CA$18.03 (13) and CA$22.19 (16), preset buttons 9.71/18.03/22.19/30/35/40, a CA$288.53 value line and the FarmLink charity.

Entering a custom price of 15 on the anchor bundle unlocks the first tier and renders exactly: 'You will get 7 items. You're missing out on Tavern Manager Simulator and 8 more! Pay at least CA$22.19 to get all items.' with a Checkout affordance.

Selecting the CA$18.03 preset renders 'You will get 13 items. You're missing out on Tavern Manager Simulator and 2 more! Pay at least CA$22.19 to get all items.' and per-item lock badges of the form 'Pay at least CA$18.03 to get this item'.
The anchor bundle's floor headline is 'Pay CA$9.71 Or More'; amounts below the floor are not a valid purchase.
The donation panel offers Default Donation / Extra to Charity / Custom Amount and shows per-party rows for Publishers, the bundle charity and Humble (observed at CA$18.03: 11.72 / 0.91 / 5.40).

/games/2k-megahits-2026-bundle is a single fixed-tier bundle at CA$21.16 unlocking 15 items against a CA$645.03 MSRP, supporting Covenant House; its unlock price is the CAD equivalent of roughly US$14.97, which is why the inventory task text names $15.
The bundles landing page listed 57 active bundles (13 games, 25 software, 19 books) in per-category mosaic order at capture time; all 13 game bundles were harvested with full tier data.
The captured bestselling order for the query 'portal' (29 results over 2 pages) and for genre=adventure (40 results) are the clone's default-sort oracles.

The header suggest panel for 'portal' returns five rows in captured order beginning with the Massive Unreal Engine Bundle row (action text 'View' plus a description line) followed by product rows carrying platform icons, discount badges and prices.
A search with no matches renders the heading '0 Results'.
An unknown deep link returns HTTP 404 with the branded copy 'THE PAGE YOU REQUESTED CANNOT BE FOUND' and intact navigation.
All captured pricing is CAD with a 'CA$' prefix because the source derives currency from the request IP (countryCode CA at capture time); the clone freezes that currency.

Sign-in offers Email, Password, an in-page 'Forgot your password?' control and Google plus Facebook SSO; registration offers Email, Password (at least 8 characters required), a newsletter checkbox, a click-to-agree Terms of Service line including mandatory arbitration, and Google SSO only.

The in-page recovery state is headed 'Password Reset' with the copy "We'll send a password setup link to your account's email address.", an Email field, a RESET PASSWORD button and a Contact Support link.
The Humble Choice marketing page priced Lite, Basic and Premium at CA$17.99 per month with an annual plan at CA$194.99 against a CA$250 base MSRP at capture time.

Every frozen page loads only local assets: the offline-clone static diagnostic reports 0 findings and 0 remote references across the 25 pages, with external navigation routed through local /external/<slug> interstitials.
544 assets are localized byte-exact from captured responses with full provenance; the only unresolved references are 10 external Steam preview videos that were intentionally not localized.

The seed is deterministic and rebuildable from the harvest: 69 store products with captured ranks, 13 fully tiered game bundles, the 57-bundle listing and the pinned suggest oracle, with all money stored as integer CAD minor units.
Checkout accepts only an opaque sandbox scenario id (sandbox-approved | sandbox-declined | sandbox-retry); payment-shaped keys are rejected before persistence and no real payment path exists.

The clone completes inventory task 671 end to end for a freshly registered account: register with email verification, open an active game bundle, set a custom price of 15, reach the checkout review showing the bundle and CA$15.00 with the charity split, place a sandbox order and receive a confirmation with revealable library keys.

A local clone-versus-source comparison of 43 checkpoint cells in the capture rendering pipeline placed 27 cells at or above 0.99 similarity and every cell at or above 0.91, with each sub-0.99 cell classified in scope/implement-notes.md.

Three-frame source calibration derived per-cell thresholds for 24 checkpoint cells; 21 are acceptance-eligible and 3 desktop cells (bundles, games, store-search) are source-limited by an entrance animation and retained as reference evidence only.
Known difference: bundle and product preview videos hosted on Steam and YouTube are not localized; posters and thumbnails render and playback is inert offline.

Known difference: the Google and Facebook SSO buttons are preserved visually but no external identity provider is reachable offline, so the clone shows a truthful local notice instead of a simulated provider flow.
Known difference: reCAPTCHA, Sift, Optimizely, Google Tag Manager, Clarity, OneTrust/Ziff Davis consent and advertising pixels are removed; the clone validates locally instead.

Known difference: the help center is frozen as three representative pages (home, the Key Redemption category and one article) under local /support routes; other categories and articles are outside the frozen subset.

Known difference: the catalog is the authorized subset (the active bundle listing in full, all 13 active game bundles in full detail, and the first two pages each of one keyword search and one category); product content is not claimed to match the live site day to day.
Known difference: books and software bundle detail pages are outside the frozen subset and return the branded 404, which is also how the source treats an expired bundle link.
Known difference: the clone always renders the captured CAD pricing, whereas the source varies currency by request region.

The bundle checkout is a single review page in two columns. The left column carries a Humble Choice offer card with an unchecked add-upsell checkbox, a Delivery Information panel naming the account the bundle will be sent to with a sign-out affordance, a Payment Method panel offering Paypal, Credit Card and Alipay radios plus a notice that the buyer is redirected to complete the purchase after continuing, a gift opt-in, and a leaderboard opt-in; its submit control reads Continue to Payment and does not advance until a payment method is chosen. The right column is an Order Summary card listing each item, Subtotal, the regional tax line (HST in the captured region), a bold Total, a charity panel naming the amount that supports the bundle's charity, and an all-caps digital-product license notice.

statement: Known difference: the store drawer's remove/undo notification is a clone addition. The source's div.cart-notifications.js-cart-notifications is present but empty in every capture (populated authenticated drawer and anonymous store drawer alike) and the only removal affordance is the one-way times-circle icon; the clone writes 'Removed <name> — Undo' with a js-hb-cart-undo control backed by /api/cart/remove + /api/cart/restore so a removal is reversible offline.

Known difference resolved in the source's favour: the captured cart has no quantity control, no quantity text and no quantity field, so the clone drawer presents none (the invented 'Qty 1' line was removed). POST /api/cart/update still accepts a qty multiplier for the seam, but no surface exposes it; T11's change-quantity clause is met by the bundle line's editable pay-what-you-want amount instead.

Known difference: in the source the drawer's Pay with Paypal (data-processor=paypal) and Pay with card (data-processor=stripe_checkout) controls hand the store cart to an external processor and /checkout is the separate bundle flow. Offline no processor exists, so both drawer controls navigate to the local review; the drawer's own giftcheckbox is rendered as captured but is not carried across that navigation.

The store cart drawer's tax line truncates rather than rounding half-up: on a CA$1.37 sub-total it shows Sales Tax CA$0.17 and a self-consistent Total CA$1.54, where 137 * 13% = 17.81 would round half-up to 18. The bundle checkout oracle ((1500-75) * 13% = 185.25 -> 185) is satisfied by both roundings and therefore never discriminated. Pinned as catalog_db.TAX_ORACLE_STORE alongside the bundle TAX_ORACLE.

The store drawer renders a 'Wallet Credit Earned' line: CA$0.14 on a CA$1.37 sub-total. The rate is the store API's own per-product rewards_split (0.1 for this product in the 2026-08-20 harvest, and for 117 of 139 harvested entries), and the captured cent is the nearest rather than the truncated one, so the rewards line rounds where the tax line truncates. The Humble Choice coupon offer in the same drawer is CA$1.95; only one cart was captured, so no scaling rule for it is claimed.

The signed-in store drawer identifies the buyer by EMAIL ADDRESS, never by display name: input.email-input.js-email is disabled and carries the address as its value with a generic your@emailaddress.com placeholder, followed by span.email 'Not <address>?' and a.logout.js-shopping-cart-logout 'Logout'. The same capture drops the 'Subscribe to hear about more deals!' checkbox and the Terms of Service paragraph that the anonymous drawer shows (both carry the source's js-newsletter-section class; zero occurrences when signed in).

Known difference: the seed is generated from the 2026-08-20 harvest, which prices bridge-constructor-portal-portal-proficiency at CA$5.53 full / CA$1.38 discounted, while the 2026-08-22 authenticated drawer capture shows CA$5.48 / CA$1.37. Both are consistent at the same captured -75% and both truncate to the same CA$0.17 tax line; the difference is a two-day CAD price refresh. The 2026-08-20 harvest stays authoritative for the catalog because tools/build_seed.py regenerates the seed byte-identically from that tracked run, and the rounding oracles are pinned on the captured 137 figures directly so the rate math is verified against the capture either way.

Known difference: the source keeps bundle purchase separate from the store cart (see claim.structural.bundle-checkout-is-separate), but this clone routes a bundle through its own cart on the way to the checkout review, so one checkout implementation serves both flows. The clone's answer to the change-quantity clause — editing a bundle line's pay-what-you-want amount in the drawer — depends on that divergence and is therefore a clone behaviour, not a source behaviour.

The signed-out navbar's Sign Up and Log In anchors are frozen as href="javascript:void(0)" and resolve to /signup?goto=<path> and /login?goto=<path>, carrying the URL-encoded pathname of the page they were activated from; there is no dropdown on either control (hover opens nothing, the click navigates).

The signed-in navbar replaces the Sign Up / Log In pair with a single user-dropdown-container holding a user-circle icon plus a caret (no display name is printed); its click-to-open panel lists Purchases, Library, Keys & Entitlements, Coupons, Wish List, Wallet, Settings and Logout in that order.

Every frozen countdown resolves to one capture instant: the detailed timers' D:H:M:S values subtracted from their bundles' end_date give 2026-08-20T22:36:58 for all nine tiles that render one (2K Megahits 01:05:23:02 against 2026-08-22T04:00:00, Excel Automation 00:19:23:02 against 2026-08-21T18:00:00, AI & Automation 01:19:23:02 against 2026-08-22T18:00:00).

A tile shows the red ticking D:H:M:S timer instead of the black 'N Days Left' pill once its day field reaches 1 (under 48h remaining). Observation bounds the cutoff rather than fixing it: every tile that rendered the red timer had at most 1d19h23m left and every tile that rendered the pill had at least 3d19h23m, and the capture contains no tile in between, so any cutoff in (43.4h, 91.4h] fits. 48h is the value the clone implements because it is the only one under which the pill never has to print the 'Days Left' label for 0 or 1 day — a form the capture never contains.

The clone anchors its countdowns to the remaining time the source rendered into the frozen markup and runs them forward from page load, so every visit starts at the captured value; it does not recompute against the absolute end dates, which by now lie in the past for the tiles that were ending soonest.
